name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q01 - Discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen

questiontext.text: The triple helical structure of collagen was discovered and published in 1954 by which of the following scientists?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the historical contribution mentioned in the text
According to the introductory overview of Unit 3, G.N. Ramachandran was an outstanding figure in protein structure and the founder of the 'Madras school' of conformational analysis of biopolymers.

Step 2: Recall the specific structural discovery
His discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen was published in Nature in 1954, which remains a landmark contribution in structural biology.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the scientist who discovered the triple helical structure of collagen is G.N. Ramachandran.

answer.text: Linus Pauling
George Palade
Camillo Golgi
G.N. Ramachandran

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q02 - Significance of the Ramachandran plot in structural biology

questiontext.text: In structural biology, the 'Ramachandran plot' developed by G.N. Ramachandran is primarily used for:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the contribution of G.N. Ramachandran
G.N. Ramachandran made foundational contributions to structural biology through conformational analysis of biopolymers.

Step 2: Analyze the role of the Ramachandran plot
The Ramachandran plot was devised specifically to analyze and describe the stereochemically allowed conformations of polypeptide chains and proteins.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the Ramachandran plot is used for analyzing the allowed conformations of proteins.

answer.text: determining the base pairing sequences in nucleic acids
measuring the rate of active transport across biomembranes
separating cell organelles based on their sedimentation coefficient
analyzing the allowed conformations of proteins

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q03 - Physicochemical approach known as reductionist biology

questiontext.text: The study and understanding of living organisms by applying the concepts and techniques of physics and chemistry to describe biological processes in molecular terms is known as:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the definition of the physico-chemical approach to life
The Unit 3 introductory text states that analyzing living tissues for elements and compounds enables one to explain physiological and behavioural processes in molecular terms.

Step 2: Identify the specific terminology
This physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms is termed 'Reductionist Biology'.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, this physico-chemical approach is known as Reductionist Biology.

answer.text: Ecological Biology
Evolutionary Biology
Morphological Biology
Reductionist Biology

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q04 - First observation and description of a live cell

questiontext.text: Who among the following scientists first saw and described a live cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the historical discovery of live cells
Section 8.1 of the textbook states that Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell under the microscope.

Step 2: Contrast with other early discoveries
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831, whereas Schleiden and Schwann formulated the cell theory, and Virchow introduced the concept of pre-existing cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek is the scientist who first saw and described a live cell.

answer.text: Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek
Robert Brown
Matthias Schleiden
Rudolf Virchow

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q05 - Discovery of nucleus as a cell organelle

questiontext.text: The nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall early observations of cellular structures
According to the NCERT text, the discovery of the nucleus within cells was achieved in 1831.

Step 2: Identify the scientist credited with the discovery
Robert Brown first described the nucleus as a distinct cellular entity in the year 1831.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by Robert Brown.

answer.text: Antonie Von Leeuwenhoek
Camillo Golgi
George Palade
Robert Brown

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q06 - Requirement of complete cellular structure for independent living

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements explains why a cell is considered the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the criteria for independent existence
Unicellular organisms are capable of independent existence and performing the essential functions of life.

Step 2: Identify the limitation of subcellular entities
The text explicitly asserts that anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living, which establishes the cell as the structural and functional baseline of life.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the fundamental nature of the cell is justified because anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living.

answer.text: Subcellular components isolated outside the cell can independently divide and reproduce indefinitely.
All metabolic reactions can occur in an abiotic environment without any cellular integrity.
Living phenomena are independent of the integrity of cellular organization.
Anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q07 - Observations of Matthias Schleiden on plant tissues

questiontext.text: In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, concluded from his studies that:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify Matthias Schleiden's professional background and observation
Matthias Schleiden was a German botanist who, in 1838, examined a large variety of plant specimens.

Step 2: Recall his specific conclusion
He observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which aggregate to form the various tissues of the plant.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Schleiden concluded that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant.

answer.text: all animal cells are delimited by an outer layer called the plasma membrane
new cells always arise de novo from non-cellular inorganic matter
the cell wall is uniquely absent in plant tissues
all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q08 - Unique character of plant cells found by Schwann

questiontext.text: Theodore Schwann (1839), based on his comparative studies on plant and animal tissues, concluded that a unique character of plant cells is the presence of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review Theodore Schwann's comparative studies
Theodore Schwann, a German zoologist, studied various animal cells and reported that they possess a thin outer layer known today as the plasma membrane.

Step 2: Identify his deduction regarding plant cells
When he extended his studies to plant tissues, he concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character distinguishing plant cells from animal cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the unique character of plant cells identified by Schwann is the presence of a cell wall.

answer.text: a cell wall
a plasma membrane
a contractile vacuole
centrioles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q09 - Contribution of Rudolf Virchow to cell theory

questiontext.text: The original cell theory formulated by Schleiden and Schwann had a major limitation because it could not explain how new cells were formed. This was resolved by Rudolf Virchow (1855), who stated:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the deficiency in Schleiden and Schwann's cell theory
The early formulation of the cell theory by Schleiden and Schwann explained that living organisms are made of cells, but failed to explain the origin or formation of new cells.

Step 2: Examine Rudolf Virchow's 1855 addition
Rudolf Virchow first explained that cells divide and that new cells arise from pre-existing cells, encapsulated in the Latin aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula'.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Virchow resolved the limitation by proposing that new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).

answer.text: cells arise spontaneously by crystallisation from extracellular inorganic fluids
plant and animal cells lack any common fundamental cellular organisation
genetic material is formed de novo inside the cytoplasm during each division cycle
Omnis cellula-e cellula, meaning that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q10 - Tenets of cell theory as understood today

questiontext.text:
Cell theory as understood today includes which of the following combined principles?
I. All living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
II. All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
III. Cells generate spontaneously from abiotic non-living matter.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the postulates of modern cell theory
Modern cell theory has two fundamental tenets: (i) all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells, and (ii) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Step 2: Evaluate statement III
Spontaneous generation from abiotic matter is completely rejected by the modern cell theory and Virchow's principle of biogenesis.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the modern cell theory comprises only statements I and II.

answer.text: Only I and III
Only II and III
I, II and III
Only I and II

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q11 - Structural boundary difference in onion and cheek cells

questiontext.text: When comparing an onion peel cell and a human cheek cell under a microscope, which outer boundary arrangement is correctly identified?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the structure of a typical plant cell (onion peel)
The onion peel cell represents a typical plant cell and possesses a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary, with the plasma membrane situated directly beneath it.

Step 2: Recall the structure of an animal cell (human cheek cell)
Human cheek cells represent animal cells and lack a cell wall; their delimiting boundary is the outer plasma membrane alone.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the onion cell has a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary with the cell membrane within it, whereas the cheek cell has an outer membrane as its delimiting structure.

answer.text: Both onion peel cells and human cheek cells have a rigid outer cell wall enclosing the plasma membrane.
The human cheek cell possesses an outer cellulosic cell wall, while the onion peel cell has only an outer plasma membrane.
Neither cell type possesses a distinct cell membrane; both are directly bounded by naked cytoplasm.
The onion cell has a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary with the cell membrane just within it, whereas the human cheek cell has only an outer membrane as its delimiting structure.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q12 - Cytoplasm as the main arena of cellular activities

questiontext.text: The semi-fluid matrix that occupies the volume of the cell and serves as the main arena of cellular activities in both plant and animal cells is the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the semi-fluid matrix filling the cell
Section 8.3 describes the semi-fluid matrix occupying the volume of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells as the cytoplasm.

Step 2: Relate it to cellular activities
Various chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm to maintain the cell in the living state, making it the primary arena of cellular metabolism.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the semi-fluid matrix acting as the main arena of cellular activities is the cytoplasm.

answer.text: cytoplasm
nucleoplasm
stroma
perinuclear space

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q13 - Locations of ribosomes in eukaryotic plant cells

questiontext.text: In a eukaryotic plant cell, ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found at which of the following intracellular sites?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the general nature and distribution of ribosomes
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound structures present in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

Step 2: Identify specific locations in plant cells from the text
Section 8.3 states: 'Within the cell, ribosomes are found not only in the cytoplasm but also within the two organelles – chloroplasts (in plants) and mitochondria and on rough ER.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, ribosomes are present in the cytoplasm, within chloroplasts, within mitochondria, and on the surface of rough ER.

answer.text: Exclusively in the cytoplasm and inside the nucleus
Only on the outer surface of smooth ER and inside the Golgi cisternae
Only inside the nucleolus and within the central vacuole lumen
In the cytoplasm, inside chloroplasts, inside mitochondria, and on the surface of rough ER

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q14 - Dimensions of Mycoplasma, typical bacteria, and human RBCs

questiontext.text:
Consider the following biological dimensions mentioned in Chapter 8:
1. Length of Mycoplasma: approximately 0.3 µm
2. Length of typical bacteria: 3 to 5 µm
3. Diameter of human red blood cells: about 7.0 µm

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Verify the dimension of Mycoplasma
Mycoplasmas are the smallest living cells, having a length of only 0.3 µm.

Step 2: Verify the dimensions of bacteria and human RBCs
Typical bacteria are 3 to 5 µm in length, and human erythrocytes (RBCs) have a diameter of approximately 7.0 µm.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, all three statements (1, 2, and 3) correctly represent the dimensions specified in the NCERT text.

answer.text: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q15 - Morphological shapes of red and white blood cells

questiontext.text: According to the description and Figure 8.1 in the text, human red blood cells and white blood cells typically exhibit which respective shapes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the shape of human red blood cells
Figure 8.1 clearly labels red blood cells as 'round and biconcave'.

Step 2: Identify the shape of white blood cells
White blood cells are illustrated and labelled as having an 'amoeboid' shape.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, red blood cells are round and biconcave, while white blood cells are amoeboid.

answer.text: Long and narrow; branched and long
Amoeboid; round and biconcave
Elongated; polygonal
Round and biconcave; amoeboid

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q16 - Four basic morphological shapes of bacteria

questiontext.text: Bacteria exhibit four basic morphological shapes. Which pairing of shape name and description is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the four basic shapes of bacteria
The text defines the four basic bacterial shapes: bacillus (rod-like), coccus (spherical), vibrio (comma shaped), and spirillum (spiral).

Step 2: Evaluate the pairings
Vibrio corresponds precisely to comma shaped, while bacillus is rod-like and coccus is spherical.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the correct pairing is Vibrio – comma shaped.

answer.text: Vibrio – comma shaped
Bacillus – spherical
Coccus – rod like
Spirillum – comma shaped

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q17 - Characteristics and phenotype conferred by bacterial plasmids

questiontext.text: In addition to the genomic DNA, many bacteria possess small circular DNA molecules called plasmids. Which of the following is a characteristic feature of plasmids?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the nature of plasmids in bacteria
Section 8.4 explains that in addition to the single circular genomic chromosome, many bacteria contain extrachromosomal small circular DNA molecules called plasmids.

Step 2: Identify the function of plasmid DNA
Plasmids confer unique phenotypic characters to host bacteria, a prime example being resistance to specific antibiotics, and are used to monitor transformation with foreign DNA.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, plasmids confer unique phenotypic characters to bacteria, such as resistance to antibiotics.

answer.text: They are enclosed inside a dedicated double-membrane envelope within the prokaryotic cytoplasm.
They are composed of linear single-stranded RNA molecules that code for ribosomal subunits.
They replace the genomic DNA during bacterial binary fission.
They confer unique phenotypic characters to bacteria, such as resistance to antibiotics.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q18 - Prokaryotes that lack a cell wall

questiontext.text: All prokaryotes possess a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane EXCEPT:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the cell boundary features of prokaryotes
Section 8.4 notes that prokaryotic cells generally have a rigid cell wall surrounding their plasma membrane.

Step 2: Identify the specific exception
The text explicitly states: 'All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, Mycoplasma is the prokaryote that lacks a cell wall.

answer.text: Blue-green algae
Bacillus
Spirillum
Mycoplasma

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q19 - Layer sequence in bacterial cell envelope from outside

questiontext.text: The chemically complex cell envelope of most bacteria consists of a tightly bound three-layered structure. What is the correct sequence from the outermost to the innermost layer?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the components of the prokaryotic cell envelope
Most bacterial cells have a tightly bound three-layered cell envelope acting together as a single protective unit.

Step 2: Determine their spatial arrangement
The outermost layer is the glycocalyx, followed by the middle cell wall, and then the innermost plasma membrane.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the sequence from outside to inside is Glycocalyx → Cell wall → Plasma membrane.

answer.text: Cell wall → Glycocalyx → Plasma membrane
Plasma membrane → Cell wall → Glycocalyx
Glycocalyx → Plasma membrane → Cell wall
Glycocalyx → Cell wall → Plasma membrane

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q20 - Classification basis of Gram positive and negative bacteria

questiontext.text: Bacteria are classified into Gram-positive and Gram-negative categories based on:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the Gram classification method
Christian Gram developed a specific differential staining technique for bacterial cells.

Step 2: Understand the structural basis of the distinction
Bacteria are classified into Gram positive (those that retain the Gram stain) and Gram negative (those that do not) based on structural and chemical differences in their cell envelopes.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the classification is based on differences in their cell envelopes and their response to the Gram staining procedure.

answer.text: differences in their cell envelopes and their response to the staining procedure developed by Gram
the presence or absence of circular genomic DNA
the sedimentation coefficient of their cytoplasmic ribosomes
the presence or absence of 9+2 axonemal microtubules in their flagella

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q21 - Distinction between slime layer and capsule in bacteria

questiontext.text: In bacteria, the glycocalyx may occur as a loose sheath called the _______ or as a thick and tough layer called the _______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the variations of the glycocalyx
Section 8.4.1 explains that the composition and thickness of the glycocalyx differ among different bacteria.

Step 2: Match the forms with their descriptive terms
When the glycocalyx is present as a loose sheath, it is called the slime layer; when it is thick and tough, it is termed the capsule.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the loose sheath is the slime layer and the thick, tough layer is the capsule.

answer.text: capsule; slime layer
mesosome; chromatophore
tonoplast; middle lamella
slime layer; capsule

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q22 - Forms and physiological functions of bacterial mesosomes

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements regarding the bacterial mesosome is INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define what a mesosome is
A mesosome is a characteristic differentiated structure formed exclusively by extensions or infoldings of the plasma membrane into the cell, not by the glycocalyx.

Step 2: Review the structural forms and functions of mesosomes
Mesosomes occur as vesicles, tubules, and lamellae. They function in cell wall formation, DNA replication, chromosome distribution during division, respiration, secretion, and expanding plasma membrane surface area.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the incorrect statement is that mesosomes are formed by infoldings of the glycocalyx layer.

answer.text: Mesosomal extensions can be in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae.
They help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and distribution to daughter cells.
They assist in cellular respiration, secretion processes, and increasing the enzymatic surface area.
Mesosomes are formed by the infoldings of the outer glycocalyx layer.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q23 - Pigment-containing membranous extensions in cyanobacteria

questiontext.text: In photosynthetic prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, membranous extensions into the cytoplasm that contain photosynthetic pigments are called:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall internal membrane structures in photosynthetic prokaryotes
Prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles such as true chloroplasts.

Step 2: Identify the specific pigment-bearing prokaryotic structure
Section 8.4.1 states: 'In some prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, there are other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called chromatophores which contain pigments.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, these membranous extensions containing pigments are called chromatophores.

answer.text: chromoplasts
chloroplasts
leucoplasts
chromatophores

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q24 - Roles of bacterial appendages in motility and attachment

questiontext.text: Which of the following correctly describes bacterial surface appendages and their roles?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze bacterial flagella structure and function
Bacterial flagella consist of three distinct parts: filament, hook, and basal body. The filament is the longest portion extending outside the cell, and flagella are responsible for motility.

Step 2: Analyze pili and fimbriae
Pili (tubular structures of special protein) and fimbriae (bristle-like fibers helping in attachment to rocks and host tissues) are non-motile surface appendages.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, flagella mediate motility while pili and fimbriae do not play a role in motility.

answer.text: Flagella are composed of filament, hook, and basal body and mediate motility, whereas pili and fimbriae do not play a role in motility.
Pili and fimbriae are primary locomotory organs that drive rapid swimming motility in water.
The basal body is the longest part of the flagellum that extends outward from the cell surface.
Fimbriae are tubular structures made of tubulin that participate in active ATP-driven locomotion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q25 - Subunits and sedimentation coefficient of prokaryotic ribosomes

questiontext.text: The prokaryotic 70S ribosome is composed of which two constituent subunits?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the subunit structure of ribosomes
Ribosomes consist of a larger subunit and a smaller subunit.

Step 2: Identify prokaryotic subunit values
Prokaryotic 70S ribosomes are formed by the association of a 50S larger subunit and a 30S smaller subunit.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the two constituent subunits of the 70S ribosome are 50S and 30S.

answer.text: 60S and 40S
50S and 40S
60S and 30S
50S and 30S

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q26 - Structure and function of polyribosomes or polysomes

questiontext.text: A chain formed when several ribosomes attach simultaneously to a single strand of mRNA is called a:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the organization of translation units
During active protein synthesis in cells, multiple ribosomes can read a single messenger RNA molecule concurrently.

Step 2: Identify the terminology used in NCERT
Section 8.4.2 states: 'Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, this chain of ribosomes attached to an mRNA is known as a polyribosome or polysome.

answer.text: mesosome
centrosome
peroxisome
polyribosome or polysome

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q27 - Non-membrane bound inclusion bodies in prokaryotic cells

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements about inclusion bodies in prokaryotic cells is INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the structure of inclusion bodies
Section 8.4.2 explicitly states: 'Reserve material in prokaryotic cells are stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm.'

Step 2: Identify membrane status
Inclusion bodies lack any bounding membrane; hence asserting that they are enclosed by a phospholipid unit membrane is incorrect.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the statement claiming inclusion bodies are surrounded by a single membrane is incorrect.

answer.text: Reserve materials in prokaryotic cells are stored in the cytoplasm as inclusion bodies.
Phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules are examples of inclusion bodies.
Gas vacuoles are found in blue-green, purple, and green photosynthetic bacteria.
They are surrounded by a single phospholipid unit membrane.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q28 - Organelles distinguishing plant cells from animal cells

questiontext.text: Plant and animal cells differ in their organelle composition. Plant cells possess _______ which are absent in animal cells, whereas animal cells possess _______ which are absent in almost all plant cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify structures unique to plant cells
Plant cells possess a rigid cell wall, plastids (such as chloroplasts), and a large central vacuole, which are absent in typical animal cells.

Step 2: Identify structures characteristic of animal cells
Animal cells have centrioles (centrosome) that aid in cell division, which are absent in almost all plant cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, plant cells possess cell walls, plastids, and a large central vacuole, whereas animal cells possess centrioles.

answer.text: cell walls, plastids, and a large central vacuole; centrioles
centrioles and lysosomes; plastids and large central vacuoles
mitochondria and 80S ribosomes; cell walls and chloroplasts
rough ER and Golgi apparatus; middle lamella and tonoplast

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q29 - Extensive compartmentalisation in eukaryotic cytoplasm

questiontext.text: Extensive compartmentalisation of the cytoplasm in eukaryotic cells is brought about by the:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand cellular compartmentalisation
Eukaryotic cells carry out numerous diverse and specialized metabolic functions simultaneously.

Step 2: Identify the structural mechanism responsible
Section 8.5 states that in eukaryotic cells, an extensive compartmentalisation of the cytoplasm is achieved through the presence of distinct membrane-bound organelles.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, compartmentalisation is achieved by the presence of membrane-bound organelles.

answer.text: presence of non-membrane bound 70S ribosomes alone
absence of a distinct nuclear membrane
folding of the genomic DNA without histone proteins
presence of membrane-bound organelles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q30 - Arrangement of phospholipids in the plasma membrane

questiontext.text: In the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane, how are the phospholipid molecules arranged, and what is the functional significance of this arrangement?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the molecular structure of membrane phospholipids
Phospholipids are amphipathic molecules containing a hydrophilic (polar) head and hydrophobic (nonpolar) hydrocarbon tails.

Step 2: Describe their orientation in the bilayer
The polar heads point towards the aqueous environments on both sides (extracellular fluid and cytoplasm), while the hydrophobic tails face inward towards each other, shielding the saturated hydrocarbon tails from water.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, polar heads are oriented towards the outer surfaces while hydrophobic tails face inward to protect saturated hydrocarbons from the aqueous environment.

answer.text: Hydrophobic tails face the outer aqueous surfaces, while polar heads are buried in the hydrophobic interior.
Both polar heads and hydrophobic tails are randomly oriented throughout the inner core of the bilayer.
Phospholipids form a single monolayer with all hydrophobic tails exposed directly to the cytoplasm.
Polar heads are oriented towards the outer surfaces, while nonpolar hydrophobic tails face the interior to protect saturated hydrocarbons from the aqueous environment.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q31 - Protein and lipid ratio in erythrocyte membrane

questiontext.text: In human beings, the plasma membrane of a mature red blood cell (erythrocyte) contains approximately:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the biochemical composition of the human erythrocyte membrane
The text discusses the chemical studies on human red blood cell membranes that helped deduce the fluid mosaic model.

Step 2: Note the specific numerical percentages
Section 8.5.1 states: 'In human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the erythrocyte membrane consists of approximately 52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids.

answer.text: 40 per cent protein and 52 per cent lipids
50 per cent protein and 50 per cent lipids
60 per cent protein and 20 per cent lipids
52 per cent protein and 40 per cent lipids

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q32 - Proponents and year of the fluid mosaic model

questiontext.text: The widely accepted 'Fluid Mosaic Model' of cell membrane structure was proposed by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the scientists who formulated the model
Section 8.5.1 clearly attributes the fluid mosaic model to S.J. Singer and G.L. Nicolson.

Step 2: Identify the year of proposal
The model was published and widely accepted in 1972.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the fluid mosaic model was proposed by Singer and Nicolson in 1972.

answer.text: Singer and Nicolson in 1972
Schleiden and Schwann in 1839
Camillo Golgi in 1898
George Palade in 1953

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q33 - Quasi-fluid nature of membrane lipids and lateral movement

questiontext.text: According to the fluid mosaic model, what enables the lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer, and what cellular functions depend on this fluidity?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the basis of membrane fluidity
The quasi-fluid state of the lipid bilayer allows dynamic lateral mobility of embedded proteins within the plane of the membrane.

Step 2: Identify physiological functions supported by fluidity
Fluidity is crucial for dynamic processes including cell growth, forming intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis, and cell division.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the quasi-fluid nature of lipids allows lateral protein mobility, facilitating cell growth, junction formation, secretion, endocytosis, and cell division.

answer.text: The rigid crystalline structure of carbohydrates enables lateral movement; functions include ATP synthesis alone.
The covalent cross-linking of peripheral proteins enables movement; functions include DNA replication only.
The static anchoring of integral proteins prevents any movement, which is essential solely for cell wall deposition.
The quasi-fluid nature of lipids enables lateral movement; functions include cell growth, formation of intercellular junctions, secretion, endocytosis, and cell division.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q34 - Transport mechanisms across selectively permeable plasma membrane

questiontext.text: Which of the following comparisons between active and passive transport across the plasma membrane is correct according to the text?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Differentiate passive and active transport mechanisms
Passive transport involves downhill movement along a concentration gradient without expenditure of cellular energy, including simple diffusion and osmosis.

Step 2: Contrast with facilitated and active transport
Polar molecules require carrier proteins because they cannot dissolve across nonpolar lipid tails. Active transport pumps ions or molecules against their gradient (from lower to higher concentration) using ATP, as exemplified by the Na+/K+ pump.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, neutral solutes move by simple diffusion down the gradient without energy, whereas active transport moves substances against the gradient using ATP, such as the Na+/K+ pump.

answer.text: Polar molecules readily cross the nonpolar lipid bilayer via simple diffusion without any carrier proteins.
Active transport always moves water molecules down their concentration gradient without utilizing ATP.
Passive transport moves solutes strictly from a region of lower concentration to higher concentration using metabolic energy.

Neutral solutes move by simple diffusion down a concentration gradient without energy, whereas active transport moves molecules against a concentration gradient utilizing ATP, as seen in the Na+/K+ pump.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q35 - Chemical composition of algal versus plant cell walls

questiontext.text: The cell wall of algae consists of _______, whereas the cell wall of other plants consists of _______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the chemical constituents of algal cell walls
Section 8.5.2 states: 'Algae have cell wall, made of cellulose, galactans, mannans and minerals like calcium carbonate...'

Step 2: Recall the chemical constituents of other plant cell walls
'...while in other plants it consists of cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins and proteins.'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, algal cell walls contain cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate, whereas other plant cell walls contain cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins.

answer.text: cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins; cellulose, galactans, mannans, and calcium carbonate
peptidoglycan and lipopolysaccharides; chitin and glucans
silica and lipid bilayer; murein and teichoic acid
cellulose, galactans, mannans, and minerals like calcium carbonate; cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and proteins

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q36 - Composition of middle lamella and function of plasmodesmata

questiontext.text: The middle lamella is a layer mainly composed of _______ that glues neighbouring plant cells together, and it is traversed by _______ which connect the cytoplasm of adjacent cells.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the chemical composition of the middle lamella
The middle lamella acts as an intercellular cementing layer made predominantly of calcium pectate.

Step 2: Identify the cytoplasmic connections
Plasmodesmata traverse the cell wall and middle lamella to connect the cytoplasm of adjacent plant cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the middle lamella consists mainly of calcium pectate and is traversed by plasmodesmata.

answer.text: calcium pectate; plasmodesmata
magnesium carbonate; desmosomes
cellulose microfibrils; tight junctions
silicon dioxide; gap junctions

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q37 - Organelles included in the endomembrane system

questiontext.text: Which group of organelles is considered together as the endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the definition of the endomembrane system
Membranous organelles whose functions are functionally coordinated are grouped into the endomembrane system.

Step 2: Identify the included and excluded organelles
The endomembrane system includes the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes are not coordinated with these and are excluded.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the endomembrane system comprises the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles.

answer.text: Endoplasmic reticulum, mitochondria, chloroplasts, and peroxisomes
Golgi complex, lysosomes, mitochondria, and ribosomes
Peroxisomes, chloroplasts, vacuoles, and centrosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, and vacuoles

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q38 - Functional differentiation between RER and SER

questiontext.text: In eukaryotic cells, the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is actively involved in _______, while the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is the major site for the synthesis of _______.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the role of RER
Rough ER has ribosomes on its surface and is extensively developed in cells actively engaged in protein synthesis and secretion.

Step 2: Recall the role of SER
Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and serves as the major site for lipid synthesis, including steroidal hormones in animal cells.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, RER is involved in protein synthesis and secretion, while SER is the site for lipid and steroidal hormone synthesis.

answer.text: lipid synthesis; proteins and glycoproteins
cellular respiration; ATP generation
ribosomal RNA synthesis; hydrolytic enzymes
protein synthesis and secretion; lipids and steroidal hormones

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q39 - Vesicle trafficking across cis and trans Golgi faces

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements correctly describes the cis and trans faces of the Golgi apparatus?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the architecture of Golgi cisternae
Golgi cisternae are arranged concentrically near the nucleus with a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face.

Step 2: Trace vesicle movement
Vesicles budded from the ER fuse with the cis face, undergo modifications within the cisternae, and are finally packaged and released from the trans face.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the convex cis face is the forming face receiving ER vesicles, and the concave trans face is the maturing face releasing modified proteins.

answer.text: The cis face is concave and releases secretory vesicles, while the trans face is convex and fuses with ER vesicles.
Both cis and trans faces are identical in morphology and function independently without interconnection.
Vesicles from lysosomes fuse with the trans face and exit through the cis face towards the nucleus.
The cis face is convex and acts as the forming face where ER vesicles fuse, while the trans face is concave and acts as the maturing face from which modified proteins are released.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q40 - Enzymatic content and optimal pH of lysosomal vesicles

questiontext.text: Lysosomes are rich in hydrolytic enzymes (hydrolases – lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) that are optimally active at:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the enzyme composition of lysosomes
Lysosomal vesicles contain diverse hydrolytic enzymes including lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases capable of digesting macromolecules.

Step 2: Recall the optimal pH environment
Section 8.5.3.3 specifies that these hydrolytic enzymes are optimally active at acidic pH.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, lysosomal enzymes are optimally active at an acidic pH.

answer.text: an acidic pH
a highly alkaline pH
a neutral pH of 7.4
a strongly basic pH above 10

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q41 - Transport across tonoplast and function of contractile vacuole

questiontext.text: Regarding vacuoles, which of the following statements is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Examine the properties of the tonoplast in plant cells
In plants, the vacuole is delimited by a single membrane called the tonoplast, which actively pumps ions against concentration gradients, resulting in significantly higher ion concentrations inside the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.

Step 2: Examine specialized vacuoles in protists
In Amoeba, the contractile vacuole plays a crucial role in osmoregulation and excretion, while food vacuoles are formed by engulfing food particles.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the tonoplast transports ions against concentration gradients into the vacuole, and the contractile vacuole in Amoeba mediates osmoregulation and excretion.

answer.text: In plant cells, ion concentration in the vacuole is always lower than in the cytoplasm due to passive leak channels.
The tonoplast is a double-membrane envelope that occupies less than 5 per cent of the plant cell volume.
Food vacuoles in Amoeba carry out osmoregulation, while contractile vacuoles digest engulfed food particles.
In plant cells, the tonoplast facilitates transport of ions against concentration gradients into the vacuole, and in Amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q42 - Function of cristae and metabolic role of mitochondria

questiontext.text: In a mitochondrion, the inner membrane forms infoldings called cristae towards the matrix. What is the primary significance of cristae?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand mitochondrial inner membrane morphology
The inner membrane of a mitochondrion folds inward toward the dense matrix, creating tubular or lamellar projections termed cristae.

Step 2: Relate cristae structure to physiological function
The cristae significantly expand the surface area of the inner membrane, which accommodates the respiratory enzymes and ATP-synthesizing complexes essential for aerobic respiration.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the primary significance of cristae is that they increase the surface area for enzymatic activities of aerobic respiration.

answer.text: They facilitate passive water diffusion into the stroma lamellae.
They serve as sites for transcription of genomic nuclear DNA.
They prevent the organelle from undergoing division by fission.
They increase the surface area available for enzymatic activities associated with aerobic respiration.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q43 - Genetic and biosynthetic components present in mitochondrial matrix

questiontext.text: The matrix of a mitochondrion possesses which of the following sets of components required for autonomous protein synthesis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify internal contents of the mitochondrial matrix
Section 8.5.4 details that the mitochondrial matrix contains single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, and ribosomes.

Step 2: Verify the ribosome sedimentation coefficient
The ribosomes inside the mitochondrial matrix are of the 70S prokaryotic type, enabling organellar protein synthesis.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the mitochondrial matrix contains a single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, 70S ribosomes, and protein synthesis machinery.

answer.text: Linear double-stranded DNA with histones, 80S ribosomes, and Golgi-derived vesicles
A single circular DNA molecule without any ribosomes or RNA molecules
Multiple linear RNA chromosomes and 60S eukaryotic ribosomal subunits
A single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, 70S ribosomes, and components for protein synthesis

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q44 - Classification of leucoplasts based on stored nutrients

questiontext.text: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store nutrients. Which of the following correctly matches the leucoplast type with its stored nutrient?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the three types of leucoplasts described in the text
Leucoplasts are non-pigmented plastids that store nutritional reserves in plants.

Step 2: Match each subtype with its specific storage product
Amyloplasts store carbohydrates such as starch (e.g., in potato); elaioplasts store oils and fats; aleuroplasts store proteins.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the correct matching is Amyloplasts – carbohydrates; Elaioplasts – oils and fats; Aleuroplasts – proteins.

answer.text: Amyloplasts – carbohydrates (starch); Elaioplasts – oils and fats; Aleuroplasts – proteins
Amyloplasts – proteins; Elaioplasts – carbohydrates; Aleuroplasts – oils and fats
Amyloplasts – oils and fats; Elaioplasts – proteins; Aleuroplasts – starch
Amyloplasts – carotenoid pigments; Elaioplasts – chlorophyll; Aleuroplasts – glycogen

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q45 - Internal organization of thylakoids and stroma in chloroplasts

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements regarding chloroplast structure is INCORRECT?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Review the internal organisation of chloroplasts
The space limited by the inner membrane is the stroma, containing stacked thylakoids (grana) connected by stroma lamellae. Chlorophyll is present in thylakoids, and the stroma contains enzymes for dark reactions, circular DNA, and ribosomes.

Step 2: Check ribosome characteristics of chloroplasts
Section 8.5.5 explicitly states: 'The ribosomes of the chloroplasts are smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ribosomes (80S).'

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the statement claiming chloroplast ribosomes are 80S is incorrect.

answer.text: Flattened membranous sacs called thylakoids are arranged in stacks called grana in the stroma.
Stroma lamellae are flat membranous tubules connecting the thylakoids of different grana.
Chlorophyll pigments are located in the thylakoids, while stroma contains enzymes for carbohydrate and protein synthesis.
Chloroplast ribosomes are 80S, identical in size to cytoplasmic ribosomes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q46 - Axonemal microtubule arrangement in cilia and flagella

questiontext.text: The core of a eukaryotic cilium or flagellum, called the axoneme, exhibits a 9+2 microtubular array. Which of the following details correctly describes its structural organization?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the 9+2 axoneme architecture
The axoneme of eukaryotic cilia and flagella has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules and a pair of centrally located microtubules (9+2 array).

Step 2: Trace the connection to the central sheath
The central tubules are enclosed by a central sheath connected to one tubule of each peripheral doublet via a radial spoke, producing nine radial spokes in total.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, the axoneme contains nine peripheral doublets, two central singlets, and nine radial spokes connecting to the central sheath.

answer.text: It has nine triplets of peripheral microtubules and no central microtubules, resembling a cartwheel hub.
It consists of two peripheral doublets and nine central microtubules linked together by pectin bridges.
Both peripheral and central tubules occur as triplets without any surrounding plasma membrane.
It has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, two centrally located singlets, and nine radial spokes connecting peripheral doublets to the central sheath.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q47 - Cartwheel organisation and triplet fibrils of centrioles

questiontext.text: In a centrosome, the two centrioles lie perpendicular to each other and exhibit a cartwheel-like organisation. Each centriole is made up of:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the structure of centrioles
Section 8.5.9 states that each centriole has an organization like a cartwheel.

Step 2: Identify the arrangement of peripheral fibrils
Centrioles are composed of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, where each peripheral fibril is a triplet, connected to a central proteinaceous hub via radial spokes.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, each centriole consists of nine evenly spaced peripheral triplet fibrils of tubulin.

answer.text: nine doublets of peripheral microtubules and two central singlet microtubules
twelve radially arranged peripheral singlets linked to an amorphous lipid core
seven peripheral triplets and two central doublets enclosed by a tonoplast
nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein, where each fibril is a triplet

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CELL_THE_UNIT_OF_LIFE_MCQ_Q48 - Classification of chromosomes based on centromere position

questiontext.text:
Based on the position of the centromere, match the chromosome type with its correct morphological description:
1. Metacentric – centromere in the middle forming two equal arms
2. Sub-metacentric – centromere slightly away from the middle forming one shorter and one longer arm
3. Acrocentric – centromere close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm
4. Telocentric – terminal centromere

Which of the descriptions are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyze the definitions of chromosome types based on centromere position
A metacentric chromosome has its centromere situated in the middle, forming two equal arms. A sub-metacentric chromosome has its centromere slightly off-center, producing one shorter arm and one longer arm.

Step 2: Evaluate acrocentric and telocentric chromosomes
An acrocentric chromosome has its centromere close to the end, yielding one extremely short arm and one very long arm. A telocentric chromosome features a terminal centromere at the very tip.

Step 3: State the final conceptual answer
Therefore, all four morphological descriptions (1, 2, 3, and 4) are completely correct.

answer.text: 1 and 2 only
1, 2, and 3 only
3 and 4 only
